subject: general
question: The second largest dome in the world was built in India and is still standing strong. Which dome is being spoken about here?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gol Gumbaz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gol Gumbaz** is the **second largest dome in the world** and is located in **Bijapur, Karnataka, India**.
 
• It was constructed in **1656** as the tomb of **Mohammed Adil Shah**, the Sultan of Bijapur.
 
• The structure is an example of **Deccan Indo-Islamic architecture**.
 
• The dome is renowned for its **whispering gallery**, where even the faintest sound gets amplified and echoes multiple times.
 
• The **diameter of the dome** is approximately **44 meters**, making it one of the largest unsupported domes globally.
 
• The building is supported by **eight intersecting arches**, which allow the massive dome to stand without support from pillars.
 
• The tomb is surrounded by a large garden area, adding to its grandeur and historical significance.
 
• The name “Gol Gumbaz” is derived from the term **‘Gola Gummata’**, meaning a circular dome in Kannada.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **GlampEco**__

 __
 
• **GlampEco** is not a historical structure or dome but refers to **eco-friendly glamping (luxury camping) accommodations**.
 
• It is unrelated to any architectural marvels or historical sites.
 
 
 
• **Teela**__
 __
 
• The term **Teela** generally refers to a **hillock or mound** in the Hindi language.
 
• It does not refer to any dome or historical monument.
 
 
 
• **Calico Dome**__
 
 
• The **Calico Dome** was an architectural structure built in **Ahmedabad, Gujarat**, in 1962.
 
• It was constructed by the **Calico Mills** and served as a showroom for their textiles.
 
• The structure was iconic for its **geodesic design** but collapsed in **2001** after the Gujarat earthquake.
